newsitem.title: UK: UK's Premier to keep focus on Far East.
newsitem.headline: UK's Premier to keep focus on Far East.

text.p: British oil and gas company Premier Oil Plc said on Thursday that it will continue its aggressive exploration programme in Indonesia following its second oil and gas discovery there this year.
"The Far East is the major area of focus," chief executive Charles Jamieson told Reuters.
"This year in Indonesia we will be drilling nine or ten wells and would expect to continue a large number there next year as well," he said.

Premier, which has been in Indonesia for around 18 months, said earlier today that it had made its second discovery in the Kakap Block since it bought an 18.75 percent interest as part of its purchase of Discovery Petroleum late last year.
The purchase of Discovery and some assets from Chevron Corp provided Premier with a position in the west Natuna area of Indonesia.
"One of the reasons for buying into this area was underlying the Natuna and Kakap field are gas accumulations," said Jamieson.
He said it was too early to be sure about the size of the latest discovery, but noted that both the recent discoveries were not "huge fields".

Testing of the latest well has been completed with stabilised flows of 7,900 barrels of oil and 1.6 million cubic feet of gas per day from the Gabus section and 300 barrels of condensate and 15 million cubic feet of gas per day from the Lama formation.
"Production should continue with these discoveries at the sort of levels we are producing at for some years to come," said Jamieson.
The well is now being suspended and fast track development plans are currently under discussion with Premier's joint venture partners.
